full_judgment: 2. The fact relevant for disposal of the rule, in short, is that the opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 299 of 1990 in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Patuakhali for declaration that the ex-parte decree on 21-1-90 in favour of defendant-petitioner in Title Suit No. 186 of 1989 in 'Ka' schedule of land in place of `Kha' schedule is illegal, collusive, fraudulent and liable to be set aside. The defendant No. 1 the petitioner, contested the suit by filing written statements denying all the material allegations made in the plaint. On 27.7.1992 the suit was posted for hearing and a petition for time on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party on that date was refused by the learned Assistant Judge who had directed the parties to be ready for hearing of the case but the plaintiff was absent when the said case was called on for hearing and that the learned Assistant Judge, Patuakhali having not found the plaintiff-opposite party had dismissed the Title Suit No. 299 of 1990. Thereafter on the same day the said opposite party had filed a petition under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the earlier order of the learned Assistant Judge and that the learned Assistant Judge had fixed 3.9.1992 for hearing the said petition. On 2.9.1992 the defendant-petitioner had filed written objection against the said prayer of the plaintiff-opposite party under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure after serving a copy to the plaintiff-opposite party alleging that there is specific remedy of the plaintiff-opposite party against the order of the learned Assistant Judge dismissing the suit for default on 27.7.92 and as such the petition for setting aside the aforesaid order dated 27.7.92 under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not maintainable in law which is liable to be rejected. On 3.1.93 the learned Assistant Judge after hearing the parties had allowed the prayer of the plaintiff-opposite party under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and passed the order for restoration of the Original Title Suit No. 299 of 1990 after setting aside his earlier order of dismissal of the suit for default dated 27.7.1992.
